summary: Sporting News writer Vinnie Iyer lays out the AFC and NFC playoff pictures after Week 13 of the 2023 NFL season, with six weeks remaining through Week 18. He walks through the seven teams currently in each conference and the key tiebreakers, then lists the teams still in the hunt. The Dolphins and Ravens lead the AFC at 9-3, while the Eagles, 49ers, Lions and Cowboys dominate the NFC.
one_line: Sporting News breaks down the AFC and NFC playoff seedings and the teams still in contention after Week 13 of the 2023 NFL season.
key_facts: Only six weeks of games remain through Week 18 after Week 13 of the 2023 NFL season.
The Miami Dolphins (9-3) hold the AFC's No. 1 seed on the conference record tiebreaker over the Baltimore Ravens (9-3) after beating the Commanders on the road.
Miami opened a 3-game AFC East lead over the idle Buffalo Bills.
The Kansas City Chiefs (8-4) are the AFC's No. 3 seed after losing to the Packers in Week 13, and have wins over the Jaguars and Dolphins for tiebreakers.
The Jacksonville Jaguars (8-4) lost at home in overtime to the Bengals on Monday night, cutting their AFC South lead to one game over Indianapolis and Houston.
The Pittsburgh Steelers (7-5) lost Kenny Pickett in a shocking home upset against the Cardinals but stay No. 5 because the Browns also lost.
The Indianapolis Colts (7-5) beat the Titans in Tennessee and don't face the Texans again until Week 18 in Indianapolis.
The Philadelphia Eagles (10-2) were routed at home by the 49ers and lead the NFC East by only one game over the Cowboys.
The San Francisco 49ers (9-3) lead the NFC West by three games over the Rams and Seahawks and are described as the new team to beat in the conference.
The Detroit Lions (9-3) lead the NFC North by 3 games after beating the Saints in New Orleans, but the No. 2 seed looks like their ceiling.
The Atlanta Falcons (6-6) lead the NFC South, the NFL's weakest division, by a full game after beating the Jets in Week 13.
The Dallas Cowboys (9-3) beat the Seahawks on Thursday night and host the Eagles in Week 14.
The Green Bay Packers (6-6) hold the final NFC wild-card spot on conference record and face the Vikings in Minnesota in Week 17.
The Texans beat the Broncos in a key wild-card matchup, and the Bengals are staying resilient without Joe Burrow.
